parties:
Gopal Chandra Shil and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh and another ------ Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
This Rule has been obtained by the defendant-petitioner challenging order dated 17-8-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. (now Joint District, Judge), 3rd Court Comilla in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 19 of 1995 whereby the judgment and order dated 24-1-1995 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Comilla in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1994 has been set aside. 

 4. Thereafter, on 10-9-1994, the Government plaintiff filed an application under Order XXII, rule 9(2) of the Code for setting aside the order of abatement dated 31-8-1994 which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1994. It has been alleged that it was not possible on the part of the government officials to keep personal knowledge regarding the death of the defendant and, as such, the government was not informed about the same nor the heirs of the deceased defendant informed the matter either before the High Court Division or before the trial Court till 10-8-1994. Thus, the plaintiff having come to know, about the death of the sole defendant on 18-8-1994 immediately filed this application for setting aside the order of abatement. The present petitioners filed objection in the said Miscellaneous Case. 

 5. The learned Assistant Judge upon consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties was pleased to reject the prayer for setting aside the order of abatement on the ground that the application filed by the plaintiff government under Order XXII, rule 9(2) of the Code is not maintainable as the same has been filed beyond the statutory period of limitation and without filing any application for condonation of delay. Moreover, the application for substitution have been filed after 10 months of the date of death without the prayer for condonation of delay as prescribed under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the application was not maintainable and, as such, the Miscellaneous Case was dismissed on contest by order dated 24-1-1995. 

 6. Against the said order the plaintiff Government preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 19 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Comilla which was ultimately heard by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) who upon hearing the parties and considering the evidences adduced by the parties allowed the appeal by his judgment and order dated 17-8-2000. Against which the present petitioners have obtained this Rule. 

 7. Mr Shishir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the present petitioners, submits that the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) committed error of law in allowing the appeal without considering that the application for substitution being filed beyond the statutory period of 90 days as prescribed in Article 177 of the Limitation Act, the same is barred by law and unless the delay is condoned under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the same cannot be allowed. Under such circumstances, the recording of abatement of the suit has been made in accordance with law. Relying on the case of Nabi Hosain and Brothers Vs Chittagong Urea Fertiliser Ltd reported in 47 DLR 473. Mr Majumder submits that the learned judge committed error of law in relying upon the evidence of PW 1, the Government Pleader's Clerk and allowing the appeal inasmuch as, it is not the function of an Advocate's clerk to swear affidavit in support of the application filed by a party posing as his Tadbirkar, his functions are rather to assist the Advocate under whom he works. A Tadbirkar and an Advocate's clerk are essentially two different persons who have different functions to perform. It must be kept in mind otherwise, the applicant will suffer. Thus he submits that the Court of appeal below upon taking into consideration the evidence of the government pleader's clerk, who is not a competent person to act on behalf of the plaintiff, has committed error in law occasioning failure of justice Relying on the case of Bhupati Biswas and others vs Niranjan Biswas and others, reported in 1989 BLD 355 = 40 DLR 517. Mr Shishir submits an abatement of a suit takes place owing to non substitution of the heirs within time resulting a vested right acquired by the defendants for not to be proceeded against in the suit. Mr Majumder then relied on the case of Hamidul Huq Chowdhury being dead his heirs, Khaled Hamidul Huq and others vs Amina Khatoon alias Roushan Ara Begum and others reported in 47 DLR 446, and submits that if a party to the suit dies, then either an application for substitution of his heirs or an application seeking exemption in accordance with Order XXII, rule 4(4)' of the Civil Procedure Code is to be filed within 90 days. A plaintiff cannot get the exemption automatically without filing an application or a Court cannot exercise the power of exemption after the suit has abated. 

 10. It is true that the abatement was recorded on 31-8-1994 and the plaintiff prayed for setting aside the order of abatement on 14-9-1994 when Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1994 was started. But the plaintiff did not pray for substitution of the heirs upon setting aside the abatement order. It was simply prayed for setting aside the abatement order recorded on 31-8-1994. 

 11. Now the question is, whether the suit abated after the expiry of 90 days of the death of a sole defendant. If that be so, then whether the suit abated on and from 8-2-1994 when 90 days expired but the heirs of deceased defendant were not substituted. Order XXII, rule 4(3) says where within the time limited by law no application is made under sub-rule (1), the suit shall abate as against the deceased defendant. Article 177 of the Limitation Act provides 90 days’ time from the date of death of the deceased defendant for substituting the heirs or legal representative in place of the deceased defendant as a party. Since the heirs of the sole deceased defendant having not been substituted in the suit within the prescribed time of 90 days i.e. by 8-2-94, the suit has abated on and from 8-2-1994 and the plaintiff having not filed an application for setting aside the order of abatement within the prescribed time of 60 days from the date of abatement i.e. 8-2-94, as prescribed under Article 171 of the Limitation Act and the plaintiff having not filed an application for substitution upon setting aside the abatement supported by an application for condonation of delay in filing the same as required under Order XXII, rule 9(3) of the Code, there is no scope of allowing such application after 10 months. Order XXII, rule 9(2) says that the plaintiff or the person claiming to be the legal representative of a deceased plaintiff or the assignee or the receiver in the case of an insolvent plaintiff may apply for an order to set aside the abatement or dismissal, and if it is proved that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from continuing the suit, the Court shall set aside the abatement or dismissal upon such terms as to costs or otherwise as it thinks fit. 

 12. From the order passed by the Court of appeal below it appears that the Court upon relying on the evidence of the clerk to the government's pleader and for the greater interest of upholding the banner of substantive justice, set aside the abatement order by order dated 31-8-1994 which upon considering the decision referred in 1989 BLD 355 is not sustainable. The effect of abatement can be overcome only by satisfying the Court as to the cause preventing the plaintiff from continuing the suit which he is under a legal obligation to do when the cause is under challenge. It is never in the discretion of the Court to allow the application for substitution either in the interest of justice or for avoiding multiplicity of proceedings. The principle relating to addition of party cannot be applied in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 16. I, therefore, find merit in this Rule and the Rule is thus made absolute. The impugned order dated 17-8-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) 3rd Court, Comilla in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 19 of 1995 is hereby set aside.
